comments.value: I'm unable to edit the post, but when I made this, I was supposed to state that these were things that I noticed with the Vive Controllers. For some weird reason, the controllers simulated Oculus controllers. The only capacitive part of the Vive wand would be the trackpad. The purpose of this post was to give suggestions to possibly remedy these issues for Vive Wands and potentially port over the features from the current set up we Vive controller users have over to other controller types, as there could be possible controllers like the Reverb G2's controllers that lack capacitive touch, or the Etee controllers which only have a trackpad. Overall would be best to think of this post as more of a consideration for future controllers

details:
From my brief time looking into the matter, I believe

# **Type: Vector2** Bindable to Thumbstick Position and TrackPad Positon

`gesture_override_axis` - This uses the Position portion of the Controller/Trackpad for gesture inputs in relation to how you're able to do it with Vive Wands. In game you should be able to access your mappings by going to `Main Menu > Settings > Controls` and you should be able to remap your gestures there, edit the area of influence, and how many gestures you want to put there.

**Gesture Axis Menu:**

Let's you map where you want things to be mapped to on a given circle/pill shaped area. You could bind the gestures to make them similar to the zones approach on the old input system and you could bind all 7 gestures on the trackpad. You can have it mirror the other controller as well or have it be independent of each controller. Image below would be some examples of potential combinations

# **Type: Boolean/Float**

`use_gesture_axis` - Allows users to put gesture overrides on a button or get around the limitations of chords. This is disabled for Oculus and Index users by default, set to `TrackPad Touch` with 

`lock_gesture_axis` - In theory should mimic the behavior of Vive Advance Settings with combining gesture weights and binding the gesture to the trigger. Takes the input from `gesture_override_axis` and binds it to the button it's assigned to. If this is disabled it will be auto enabled

`enable_rotate` - a boolean that takes position data of the trackpad/thumbstick if you press a button. Default binding should be set to `Right Thumbstick: Touch` on Oculus Touch and Index Controllers, and `Right Trackpad: DPad East` + and `Right Trackpad: DPad West`on Vive Wands. If disabled it will auto configure to the current touch behavior in the beta.

`enable_move` - same idea/behavior as `enable_rotation` with movement/locomotion. 

# Skeletal input default bindings for Non-Index controllers

Skeletal Input should be accessible in the `global` section for all controllers only because default in game behavior will have users use `gesture_direct_open`. This is fine for Oculus users, however not for Vive Controller users. Defaults for Oculus controllers should be `gesture_direct_open` while default Vive controller users should use `disable_gesture_track`
